name: Apolipoprotein A-I
rangeNote: The app has no universal range for ApoA-I. It uses the laboratory's range when supplied; interpretation also depends on the rest of the lipid results and overall heart risk.
summary: Apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA-I) is the main protein in high-density lipoprotein (HDL), which helps move cholesterol out of cells. The test measures the amount of this protein, not how well HDL works. A higher result does not by itself prove protection from heart disease.

high.meaning: Higher ApoA-I is often seen alongside higher HDL, but more is not automatically better. Raising ApoA-I has not been shown to reliably prevent heart attacks; discuss a result outside the laboratory's range with your doctor.
commonCauses: Differences in the production and breakdown of HDL particles
Alcohol use, which can raise ApoA-I without making alcohol a way to protect the heart

low.meaning: Lower ApoA-I can accompany a less favourable lipid pattern or inflammation. It does not diagnose heart disease or identify a cause on its own; discuss a result below the laboratory's range with your doctor.
commonCauses: Genetic differences affecting ApoA-I production and HDL metabolism

sources.title: Apolipoprotein A1 Infusions and Cardiovascular Outcomes after Acute Myocardial Infarction.
